passage: I am Hrithik, and I was waiting at the park gate when Pankaj, about two, took off across the grass, grinning. He stopped, looked back over his shoulder at his mother, and squealed. She jogged after him, arms out, and he ran again, shrieking, checking her face each time. I cannot know for sure what he meant, but he seemed to be asking her to chase.

qa.q: Where was Hrithik waiting?
qa.a: He was waiting at the park gate.

qa.q: What does Pankaj's look back over his shoulder suggest, and what else might it mean?
qa.a: It suggests he is inviting his mother to chase and enjoying the game. It might also be checking that she is still near.

qa.q: What can an adult do when a toddler runs and looks back like this?
qa.a: They can join in with a playful chase, then let the toddler chase them back, which builds connection and turn-taking.

qa.q: How might Pankaj's mother feel about the game?
qa.a: She may feel a bit tired but also delighted, since he wants to play with her.

grounding: A toddler runs away with a grin and looks back to invite a chase.

passage: On Monday Trisha, two, ran down the hallway and stopped, looking back with a grin. Ojas dropped his phone and chased her, growling in play. On Thursday Ojas was busy cooking; Trisha ran, looked back, and when nobody came she stopped smiling and came to tug his trouser leg. "Sorry, chase after dinner," he said. On the next Sunday he ran, looked back and waited; Trisha chased him, shrieking with laughter.

qa.q: What did Trisha do on Thursday when nobody chased her?
qa.a: She stopped smiling and came to tug at Ojas's trouser leg.

qa.q: What might Trisha have felt when nobody came on Thursday, and what else could explain her tugging?
qa.a: She was probably let down when her invitation was not answered. She may also have simply wanted her father's attention.

qa.q: What could Ojas do when he is busy?
qa.a: He can answer her look with a quick word and a promise for later, then keep it, as he did on Sunday. 🙂

qa.q: How might Ojas feel when Trisha tugs his trouser leg on Thursday?
qa.a: Ojas may feel a little torn between cooking and playing, but he answers her kindly and promises a chase after dinner.

grounding: A toddler runs away with a grin and looks back, and adults who join in build connection and turn-taking.

passage:
Fresh out of the bath in their Pune flat, Jagdish wriggled free of the towel and ran down the corridor, giggling. At the bedroom door he stopped and looked back over his shoulder, grinning at Hemant.
"I'm coming to get you!" Hemant said, taking big slow steps.
Jagdish shrieked, ran behind the curtain, and peeped out again, waiting.

qa.q: Where did Jagdish hide?
qa.a: Behind the curtain.

qa.q: What did Jagdish's look back over his shoulder mean?
qa.a: It was an invitation to play; he felt playful and excited and wanted Hemant to chase him.

qa.q: What did Hemant do that built connection?
qa.a: He accepted the invitation and chased with big slow steps, keeping the game fun and safe.

qa.q: What would change if Hemant had just scolded him to come back and dress?
qa.a: Jagdish would miss the playful connection, and getting dressed might have turned into a struggle.

grounding: A toddler runs off grinning and looks back to be chased, and his father joins the game.

passage:
"She's running away from me again!" said Dadi, puffing.
Sabina stopped at the end of the hall and looked back, grinning.
"Look, she's waiting," said Kalyani, her mother. "She wants you to chase her."
"Oh! I'm coming, I'm coming!"
Sabina squealed and ran. At the wall she turned round, and this time ran at Dadi.
"Now you're chasing me?" Dadi laughed, and turned to run.

qa.q: Who chased Sabina?
qa.a: Dadi.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when she looked back grinning?
qa.a: She was playful and happy, inviting Dadi to chase her.

qa.q: How did Kalyani help Dadi understand Sabina?
qa.a: She pointed out that Sabina's look back meant she wanted to be chased, not that she was running away.

qa.q: How might Dadi feel when Sabina turns to chase her?
qa.a: Dadi likely feels delighted and amused, enjoying the turn-taking game.

grounding: A mother helps a grandmother see that a toddler's grinning look back is an invitation to chase, building turn-taking.

passage: Childminder's note, Tuesday. In the garden, Rashmi ran off toward the hedge, then stopped and looked back at me with a huge grin. I took the hint and chased her, slowly, saying "I'm going to catch you!" She shrieked. After a few rounds, she stopped, turned round and ran after me instead. We took turns until snack time. She is starting to understand the game goes both ways. Nirmala, childminder

qa.q: What did Rashmi do after a few rounds?
qa.a: She stopped, turned round and ran after Nirmala instead.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling when she looked back with a grin?
qa.a: She felt playful and excited, and was inviting Nirmala to chase her.

qa.q: What did Nirmala's joining in help Rashmi learn?
qa.a: Turn-taking, since the chasing game went both ways.

qa.q: How might Rashmi's parents feel reading the note?
qa.a: They would likely feel happy to hear she had such fun and is learning to take turns.

grounding: A childminder joins a toddler's look-back chasing game, and they take turns.

passage:
Between the tea bushes behind their house in the Assam village, Bhupen suddenly ran off, grinning, his little legs pumping. After a few steps he stopped and looked back over his shoulder at his uncle Santosh.
“I'm coming to get you!” Santosh stomped after him.
Bhupen shrieked with joy and ran again, looking back every few steps.
When Santosh caught him, Bhupen wriggled free, pointed at him, and started chasing Santosh instead.

qa.q: Where did Bhupen run off?
qa.a: Between the tea bushes behind their house.

qa.q: What did Bhupen want when he looked back over his shoulder?
qa.a: He wanted Santosh to chase him; the grin and look back were a playful, excited invitation to the game.

qa.q: How did Santosh build connection with Bhupen?
qa.a: He read the look back as an invitation and joined in, and then let Bhupen take his turn as the chaser.

qa.q: How might Santosh feel being chased by Bhupen?
qa.a: He probably feels amused and close to Bhupen, enjoying the swap of turns.

grounding: It shows a toddler running off with a grin and looking back to be chased, and an adult joining in and swapping turns.
